protocols.section_text: Organ Constraints* Additional information Spinal cord D0.1% <48 Gy Relevant if extended field or para-aortic treatment is used. Contour the bony spinal canal. Small bowel/peritoneal cavity Apply ALARA principles and avoid hotspots where possible. No lymph node involvement: Ideal: V40 Gy <250 cm³ Ideal: V30 Gy <500 cm³ Acceptable: D0.1% <105% Involved lymph nodes, without para-aortic irradiation: Ideal: V40 Gy <250 cm³ Ideal: V30 Gy <500 cm³ Acceptable: D0.1% <105% in regions outside 10-15 mm from the involved nodal PTV. Involved lymph nodes, with para-aortic irradiation: Ideal: V40 Gy <300 cm³ Ideal: V30 Gy <650 cm³ Acceptable: D0.1% <105% in regions outside 10-15 mm from the involved nodal PTV. Peritoneal cavity: Includes the volume surrounding the small bowel loops, extending to the peritoneal edge, as the bowel may occupy this space at any point during treatment. r Exclude the CTV. Sigmoid No lymph node involvement: Acceptable: D0.1% <105% Involved lymph nodes: Acceptable: D0.1% <105% in regions outside 10-15 mm from the involved nodal PTV. Bladder No lymph node involvement: Ideal: V40 Gy <60% Ideal: V30 Gy <80% Acceptable: D0.1% <105% Involved lymph nodes: Ideal: V40 Gy <60% Ideal: V30 Gy <80% Acceptable: D0.1% <105% in regions outside 10-15 mm from the involved nodal PTV. Contour entire external outline of bladder wall, including the bladder neck. Rectum No lymph node involvement: Ideal: V40 Gy <75% Ideal: V30 Gy <95% Acceptable: D0.1% <105% Involved lymph nodes: Ideal: V40 Gy <75% Ideal: V30 Gy <95% Acceptable: D0.1% <105% in regions outside 10–15 mm from the involved nodal PTV. Contour from the anorectal sphincter to the rectosigmoid junction. Femoral heads Acceptable: D0.1% <50 Gy Contour from superior edge of acetabulum to lesser trochanter. Kidney Ideal: Dmean <10 Gy Acceptable: Dmean <15 Gy Consider split renal perfusion scan if concerned about kidney dose. Relevant if extended field or para-aortic treatment is used. Bone marrow Ideal: V10 Gy <80% r Ideal: V20 Gy <66% r Acceptable: V10 Gy <90% r Acceptable: V20 Gy <75% r Optional structure. Contour the pelvic bone as a surrogate for bone marrow. Include femoral heads but not femoral necks. Body/external contour No lymph node involvement: Acceptable: D0.1% <107% Involved lymph nodes: Acceptable: D0.1% <107% in regions outside 10-15 mm from the involved nodal PTV. Vagina (if not involved) Acceptable: PIBS-2cm <5 Gy Optional dose reporting point. PIBS refers to the posterior-inferior border of the symphysis pubis. Transposed ovaries Ideal: Dmean <5 Gy Acceptable: Dmean <8 Gy Optional structure. Consider only in selected premenopausal patients where ovarian transposition is relevant. In case of ovarian transposition delineate outer contour of ovary. Duodenum Acceptable: V55 Gy <15 cm³ r Relevant if extended field or para-aortic treatment is used. * OAR constraints are based on the EMBRACE II study protocol (v1.0, Table 9.4, 2018 update) unless stated otherwise. r Refer to the original publication for further guidance. Note: Where a dose is expressed as a percentage (e.g. D0.1% <105% or D0.1% <107%), the percentage is relative to the main prescription dose unless otherwise specified. OAR notes OAR constraints should be prioritised according to the risk of clinically significant toxicity, target coverage requirements, and individual patient factors. Where ideal OAR constraints are listed these should not be prioritised over adequate target coverage. Recommended contouring guidelines Suggested contouring atlas are available at NRG oncology - Gynaecologic Cancer Atlases, Templates, & Tools . The EMBRACE II cervical cancer protocol provides detailed guidance for contouring primary targets, involved and elective nodal volumes, and OAR. r

protocols.section_text: High conformal modulated treatment technique Organ Constraint Notes Lung Mean dose <8 Gy r r r For hypofractionated schedules (>2 Gy per fraction), consider adjusting constraint to maintain a mean <8 Gy EQD2. Kidneys Mean dose <8-10 Gy r r r Both kidneys combined. Lens Max dose ≤90% prescribed dose r Prioritise preservation of optic nerve and central nervous system (CNS) volume coverage. r OAR notes For conventional treatment techniques: Appropriate shielding should be used to achieve a dose to the lung and kidney that is as low as reasonably achievable (ALARA) for the treatment technique used. For highly conformal modulated treatment techniques: There are various OARs that may be considered during treatment planning e.g. heart, brain, thyroid, testes, liver, oesophagus, oral cavity, rectum, pancreas and stomach. Reducing dose to these structures is optional and should be balanced against the risk of relapse. r Additional structure contours may be used to evaluate dose to specific target or OAR structures e.g. ribs, testes, areas of cerebrospinal fluid extension on the cribriform plate and/or optic nerves. Planning organ at risk volume (PRV) For highly conformal modulated treatment technique: For OARs susceptible to breathing motion and volume-changes, consider the use of PRV structures to reduce OAR doses while maintaining target dose coverage e.g. lungs minus a 5 mm internal margin to reduce lung dose while maintaining dose to ribs. r

OAR notes Doses listed here are from the CHHiP trial and reflect the OAR contours described within the trial protocol. When applying these constraints to a clinical setting, clinicians should consider the significant variation between contouring guidelines in this trial and within individual institutions. These constraints are based on the currently available evidence from clinical trials when modulated planning techniques and implanted rectal spacers were not widely used. The reference committee strongly recommends that treating clinicians consider improving on these constraints based on departmental and patient-specific factors.
